Single-sample Bayesian regression (reference estimators)

Source: R/baseline.R, R/methods.R
baseline_fit.Rd

Fits the target regression model alone, with the same priors and the same MCMC updates as the target component of mixture_fit(), but without any contamination component. It reproduces the original baseline functions fit_bayes_lm(), fit_bayes_logit() and fit_bayes_pois() and is useful to compare

  • the probability-only estimator (data = prob_data), and

  • the naively pooled estimator (data = rbind(prob_data, nonprob_data)), which treats every NP unit as compatible,

with the contamination-aware fit.

Usage

baseline_fit(
  formula,
  data,
  family = c("gaussian", "binomial", "poisson"),
  n_iter = 2000,
  burnin = 1000,
  thin = 1,
  seed = NULL,
  prior = mixture_prior(),
  control = mixture_control(),
  na_action = c("omit", "fail")
)

baseline_fit_matrix(
  x,
  y,
  family = "gaussian",
  n_iter = 2000,
  burnin = 1000,
  thin = 1,
  seed = NULL,
  prior = mixture_prior(),
  control = mixture_control()
)

# S3 method for class 'bsm_baseline'
summary(object, level = 0.95, ...)

# S3 method for class 'summary.bsm_baseline'
print(x, digits = 3, ...)

# S3 method for class 'bsm_baseline'
print(x, digits = 3, ...)

# S3 method for class 'bsm_baseline'
coef(object, ...)

Arguments

formula

A two-sided model formula, e.g. y ~ x1 + x2. Offsets are not supported.

data

Data frame containing the variables in formula.

family

One of "gaussian", "binomial" (logistic regression for a 0/1, logical or two-level factor response) or "poisson". A family object such as binomial() is also accepted (only its name is used; the links are fixed to identity, logit and log respectively).

n_iter, burnin

Total iterations (including burn-in) and burn-in; the defaults (2000, 1000) are those of the original baseline functions.

thin

Keep every thin-th post-burn-in draw.

seed

Optional random seed. When supplied the fit is reproducible and the global random-number stream is restored afterwards; when NULL the current stream is used.

prior

Prior hyperparameters, see mixture_prior().

control

Algorithm settings, see mixture_control().

na_action

"omit" (default) drops rows with missing values in any model variable, separately within each sample, and records how many were dropped; "fail" stops with an error if any are present.

x

For baseline_fit_matrix(), the design matrix; for the print methods, a bsm_baseline or summary.bsm_baseline object.

y

Response vector (matrix interface).

object

A bsm_baseline object.

level

Credible-interval level for summary().

...

Not used.

digits

Significant digits for printing.

Value

An object of class bsm_baseline with elements draws, coef_names, family, acceptance (Poisson only), mcmc and the information needed by predict().

Examples

d <- simulate_mixture_data("gaussian", n_prob = 80, n_nonprob = 80,
                           contamination = 0.4, seed = 2)
prob_only <- baseline_fit(y ~ x1, d$prob, n_iter = 600, burnin = 200, seed = 1)
pooled <- baseline_fit(y ~ x1, rbind(d$prob, d$nonprob[names(d$prob)]),
                       n_iter = 600, burnin = 200, seed = 1)
rbind(prob_only = coef(prob_only), pooled = coef(pooled))
#>           (Intercept)       x1
#> prob_only    2.077655 4.885738
#> pooled       1.697441 2.774794
